title: Explorer page resolution
responsibility: Resolves console paths into canonical redirects, revision-scoped pages or explicit missing results.

inputs.name: homePath.index
inputs.description: The history index the home is chosen from, read for its branches (name and head) and revisions (commit): the first branch named main or master whose head is one of its revisions, else the first branch whose head is one, else the commit of its first revision. It matters because a missing result links to that home and the root redirects to it unless its query names a commit the index holds, and the home is null only when the index lists no revision.

revisions.subject: Add the explorer scope resolver
revisions.author: Grace Hopper
gaps: no verification record is attached to this commit

inputs.name: harnessPage.index
inputs.description: The history index the path is resolved against: its branches (name and head) and the commits and branches of its revisions decide the redirect, page or missing result, and a page shows the full summary of its revision, with its parents and records. An explorer address in canonical form that names a branch or commit the index does not hold is missing, while an address in another form redirects first, and a console page that names a commit it does not hold redirects to the home.

revisions.subject: Add the explorer scope resolver
revisions.author: Grace Hopper
gaps: no verification record is attached to this commit

inputs.name: harnessPage.path
inputs.description: The console path to resolve, which begins with `/` (the root is `/` or an empty string) and may end in slashes, which are ignored. A path without the leading `/` is not read as written, because the explorer drops the first segment before it.

inputs.name: harnessPage.search
inputs.description: The query string that goes with the path, read as URLSearchParams so a leading `?` is optional: an entity address reads its `tab` and `helper` keys, the root or an earlier console page reads its `commit`, `view` and `unit` keys, and other addresses ignore it. It defaults to an empty string, which carries no query.

outputs.name: homePath
outputs.description: The canonical home route: `/branch/<name>/pages`, with the branch name URL-encoded, when a branch head is one of the revisions, else `/commit/<sha>/pages` for the first revision. It is `null` only when the index lists no revision, and it is the route the explorer opens at.

outputs.name: harnessPage
outputs.description: One of three shapes: a `redirect` to the canonical explorer path the address stands for, a `page` whose `scope` is the addressed commit (the branch tip when only a branch is named), or a `missing` result with a `message` and the `home` link. An address that names only a commit on a branch redirects to that branch's address, while the root of a history with no revision, an address that names no page, and a canonical explorer address whose branch or commit the index does not hold are `missing`, never shown in its place.

examples.message: Commit 9d3f2a1 is not in this history.
